name: Point Nepean National Park
bio_draft: southern tip of the peninsula with Fort Nepean, beaches, walks and the Quarantine Station.

facts.claim: Park at the very tip of the Mornington Peninsula near Portsea, with historic Quarantine Station buildings, military forts and tunnels
Walking and cycling tracks with ocean and bay views; the memorial and site where Prime Minister Harold Holt went missing at Cheviot Beach
Hop-on-hop-off shuttle runs between the Quarantine Station and Fort Nepean
560 ha park, open daily; vehicles enter 6am-6pm

name: Peninsula Hot Springs
bio_draft: mineral bathing complex at Fingal with thermal pools and spa.

facts.claim: Geothermal mineral springs and day spa at Fingal, less than 90 minutes from Melbourne
Over 70 bathing and wellness experiences in a natural landscape; Bath House (all ages) and adults-only Spa Dreaming Centre (16+)
Bath House bathing from about $60 to $90 per adult depending on session

name: Cape Schanck Lighthouse
bio_draft: working lightstation at the tip of the peninsula on Bass Strait, with its reserve and rock views.

facts.claim: Limestone lighthouse built in 1859 at Cape Schanck, the southernmost tip of the Mornington Peninsula; 21 m tall and still active
Retains its original 1859 Chance Brothers Fresnel lens and an early clockwork mechanism
Guided tower climbs and a museum in the keeper's red brick house; museum entry by donation
Reserve sits within Mornington Peninsula National Park, with coastal walks

name: Fort Nepean
bio_draft: 19th-century coastal fort in Point Nepean National Park, open to visitors with guided and self-guided access.

facts.claim: Fortification at the very end of the Mornington Peninsula that protected Port Phillip and Melbourne in WWI and WWII
Extensive tunnel complex connecting the historic gun emplacements
Within Point Nepean National Park; reached by the hop-on-hop-off shuttle from the Quarantine Station, by bike or on foot

name: Mornington Peninsula National Park
bio_draft: strip of ocean beaches, cliffs and bushland from Point Nepean to Cape Schanck, with walks and surf beaches.

facts.claim: Wild ocean beaches between Portsea and Flinders, plus Greens Bush, the largest remnant of native bushland on the peninsula
Surf beaches at Gunnamatta, Flinders, Portsea and Rye; rockpools at Sorrento Ocean Beach
The Coastal Walk is a two-day clifftop walk; the Two Bays Walking Trail is 26 km from Dromana to Cape Schanck
Dogs are not permitted anywhere in the park

unresolved: no fee stated on page; free assumed (Victorian national park)

name: Sorrento
bio_draft: historic seaside town where Victoria's first settlement was founded in 1803, with ocean and bay beaches and the ferry to Queenscliff.

facts.claim: Seaside town where the British set up a convict settlement in 1803 under David Collins, the first British settlement on mainland Australia outside the Sydney region
Sits between ocean and bay beaches; Sorrento Ocean Beach rockpools are in Mornington Peninsula National Park
Passenger and vehicle ferry runs from Sorrento to Queenscliff

name: Red Hill
bio_draft: rolling hills with the peninsula's main cellar doors, cheese producers and a community market.

facts.claim: Red Hill is a rural town on the Mornington Peninsula, about 92 km from Melbourne.
Wineries have been established around Red Hill since the 1970s, taking advantage of microclimates suited to cool-climate grapes, especially pinot noir.
Strawberries, cherries and apples are grown here and sold seasonally at the farm door.
A monthly community market runs from September to May.

access_note: Community market site (redhillcommunitymarket.com.au) shows 'Temporarily closed'; market is monthly so should not be a headline in the bio.

name: Two Bays Walking Trail
bio_draft: 26 km trail from Dromana to Cape Schanck through Arthurs Seat and the national park.

facts.claim: A 26 km hike from Dromana to Cape Schanck through Arthurs Seat State Park and Mornington Peninsula National Park.
Beyond Arthurs Seat the walk is relatively flat, through eucalypt forest and grassy Greens Bush to coastal cliffs near Cape Schanck.
It suits a two-day hike, a long day hike or section by section, and is marked with a Blue Wren symbol.

name: Coastal Walk (Mornington Peninsula)
bio_draft: two-day coastal walk along the clifftops of Mornington Peninsula National Park, Portsea to Flinders.

facts.claim: A two-day walk through Mornington Peninsula National Park along high clifftops, coastal vegetation and past ocean beaches.
The national park spans the wild ocean beaches between Portsea and Flinders.

unresolved: Walk length and exact route (Portsea to Cape Schanck vs to Flinders) not stated on fetched page; no separate Parks Victoria walk page found

name: Bushrangers Bay
bio_draft: bay in Mornington Peninsula National Park reached by a walk of about 20 minutes, with kangaroos along the way.

facts.claim: The Bushrangers Bay Walk starts at the eastern car park at Cape Schanck Lighthouse and drops to a sandy beach ringed by basalt cliffs, at the outlet of Main Creek.
It is a 5.4 km return walk of about 2 hours on sandy unsealed paths with steep stairs.
Rockpools can be explored at low tide, and the Main Creek estuary may need wading when the tide is in.
Swimming is not recommended: the beach is unpatrolled with rips and strong currents.

access_note: Bio draft's '20 minutes' and 'kangaroos' conflict with the agency: 2 hours return from Cape Schanck Lighthouse. Fix the bio.

name: Arthurs Seat State Park
bio_draft: hill reserve above Dromana with summit views, walking tracks, mountain-bike trails and the Two Bays Trail start.

facts.claim: The 314 m summit gives views that on a clear day reach the Melbourne skyline, the You Yangs and Mount Macedon.
The park has walking and mountain-bike tracks, a circuit walk to Kings Falls and Seawinds Garden with William Ricketts sculptures.
The Arthurs Seat Eagle gondola, run separately, rises above the trees; the Two Bays Walking Trail passes through the park.

access_note: Eagle gondola (separate operator, about $29.90 adult return per operator's ticket page) is an extra, not the spot's price. Operator site not loaded (arthursseateagle.com.au fetch failed).

name: Flinders Blowhole
bio_draft: blowhole on the rocks at Flinders, reached by a walking track in the national park.

facts.claim: The blowhole is on the Flinders coast, viewed from a small lookout high on a headland above the rock shore.
A short steep track with many steps leads from the car park down to the shoreline and rockpools.
The blowhole is best seen working at low tide; swimming is not recommended because of rips and large waves.

name: Portsea Surf Beach
bio_draft: ocean surf beach on the tip of the peninsula at Portsea, inside the national park.

facts.claim: Portsea Surf Beach is an ocean beach within Mornington Peninsula National Park, on the Bass Strait side of Portsea.
Portsea, Sorrento and Gunnamatta surf beaches are patrolled during summer holidays.
Parks Victoria lists it among the national park's surf beaches for surfing, swimming and rockpool exploring.

unresolved: No fee shown on the Parks Victoria page; Victorian national parks are free to enter

name: Gunnamatta Beach
bio_draft: back-beach surf break in Mornington Peninsula National Park, named as a surfing beach by Wikivoyage.

facts.claim: Gunnamatta Beach is a surf beach in Mornington Peninsula National Park, noted by Parks Victoria as a draw for experienced surfers.
Gunnamatta is one of the park's ocean beaches along with Flinders, Portsea and Rye.
Patrolled during summer holidays.

name: Coolart Wetlands and Homestead
bio_draft: waterbird wetlands on Western Port with a historic homestead and gardens near Somers.

facts.claim: Coolart is a wetlands reserve and historic homestead at 40 Lord Somers Rd, Somers, on Western Port Bay.
The wetlands are open daily; the homestead and shop open Wednesday, Saturday and Sunday only.
Dogs are not permitted, under Parks Victoria regulations.
The site has a community garden and rose garden around the homestead.

access_note: Homestead open only Wed, Sat, Sun; wetlands daily

name: Mornington
bio_draft: largest town on the peninsula, a main street running down to the beach and pier, with cafes and the Mornington Racecourse.

facts.claim: Mornington is the largest town on the peninsula's Port Phillip side, with a main street running down to the pier and foreshore.
Its Mornington Racecourse is in the town.
It is the main shopping and cafe centre of the eastern peninsula.

unresolved: Facts from the Wikipedia article only; confirm town-centre pin vs. the existing placement point

name: McCrae Homestead
bio_draft: National Trust homestead at Rosebud, a historic house run by the National Trust.

facts.claim: McCrae Homestead was home to artist Georgiana McCrae, who arrived in 1845 and drew the plan for the house herself.
It gives a view of domestic life in the 1840s.
The Burrell Gallery in the homestead tells a family's story on the Mornington Peninsula over 75 years.
It is run by the National Trust and sits at 11 Beverley Road, McCrae.

name: The Briars
bio_draft: National Trust homestead and wildlife sanctuary at Mount Martha, with history and walking tracks.

facts.claim: The Briars is one of the oldest homesteads on the Mornington Peninsula, surrounded by a wildlife sanctuary and vineyards.
Napoleon memorabilia collected by Dame Mabel Brookes, including Bonaparte's writing table, is displayed in the homestead.
The precinct has a visitor centre, wetlands, gardens, cafe and picnic areas with free BBQs.
Entry to the park is free.

name: Rye Ocean Beach
bio_draft: ocean surf beach at Rye, inside the national park, listed as a surfing beach.

facts.claim: Rye Ocean Beach lies in the heart of Mornington Peninsula National Park's coastline.
Powerful waves and numerous reef breaks make it popular with experienced surfers.
Visitors can walk the exposed sandy shoreline, look out across Bass Strait and spot shorebirds.

name: Coppins Track
bio_draft: coastal track above Sorrento Ocean Beach in Mornington Peninsula National Park.

facts.claim: Coppins Track is near Sorrento and overlooks Sorrento Ocean Beach, with stairs to a lookout platform.
It winds through coastal scrub along the coast to Diamond Bay.
A round trip starts and finishes at Sorrento Ocean Beach, which has toilets, barbecues, a cafe and a patrolled surf beach.

name: Mushroom Reef Marine Sanctuary
bio_draft: rocky reef marine sanctuary off Flinders Ocean Beach, for snorkelling and rockpools.

facts.claim: The 80 ha sanctuary at Flinders takes its name from its mushroom-shaped reef and extends about 1 km offshore.
Rockpools at Flinders are good for exploring Victoria's marine life, and snorkelling and diving on the subtidal reefs is popular.
All fishing and taking of animals, plants and artefacts is prohibited.

name: Alba Thermal Springs & Spa
bio_draft: day spa with thermal pools on the peninsula, listed as a favourite by the regional tourism board; spa is a commercial venue.

facts.claim: Alba is a hot-springs and spa wellness destination on the Mornington Peninsula, set in native bushland.
It has outdoor geothermal pools including a rain pool and forest pools.
Private rooftop geothermal pools and spa treatments are also offered.

name: Penguin Parade
bio_draft: nightly sunset parade of little penguins returning to nests at Summerland, run by Phillip Island Nature Parks.

facts.claim: Phillip Island is home to the largest little penguin colony in the world.
Penguins waddle home from the sea to their burrows at sunset every night of the year, watched from viewing platforms and boardwalks.
Tickets should be booked in advance; ticket holders should arrive about an hour before penguin arrival time.
It is run by Phillip Island Nature Parks at Summerlands Beach.

access_note: Booking essential; upgrade works to burrows and boardwalks underway. Price is General Viewing adult (16+) $34; premium tiers $85-$129.

name: Koala Conservation Centre
bio_draft: tree-top boardwalks to see wild koalas in the eucalypts, run by Phillip Island Nature Parks.

facts.claim: Two tree-top boardwalks (800 m and 600 m loops, about 20 minutes each) give close views of koalas in their natural habitat.
Six hectares of bushland trails also have wallabies, echidnas and native birds.
Run by Phillip Island Nature Parks; the operator now calls it the Koala Conservation Reserve.

access_note: Self-guided adult $17.50; guided tour $60. Operator name is now 'Koala Conservation Reserve' - consider renaming. Wikipedia title 'Koala Conservation Centre' redirects to Phillip Island Nature Park, so wiki null.
